e.text: A3 hits 20.1%, triple the benchmark; asking the Critic how to push it and A2 further.

e.note: Reading results for A3, A2, A1

critique.summary: A3 is the strongest plan at 20.1% reach (P10 17.6%) for $694 per point, about 2.7x cheaper than the benchmark's $1895, driven by the Airbnb drop, city-wide social and Rich Roll. The day-40 Seven Sins pop-up ($2500 for 0.4% of credited adoption) and zone-only ads in A1 are poor value, and Fortnite/reggaeton and Stranger Things/K-pop districts lag at 16.6%.

findings.finding: Highest reach at 20.1% (P10 17.6%, above every other plan's mean except A2's ceiling) for $694 per point; the Airbnb drop earns 14.1% of credited adoption on just $2000.
The popup:33C041EA on day 40 costs $2500 but earns only 0.4% of credited adoption, too late for word of mouth to spread.
Reaches 16.4% (P10 14.4%) at $881 per point; without the Airbnb drop it trails A3 despite spending $530 more, though The Minimalists still earned 7.1% for $3350.
Reaches only 13.2% at $944 per point; zone ads in Narvarte and Santa María ($2460 each) earn just 1.5% each, and Fortnite/reggaeton reaches only 8.3%.
Reaches 6.7% at $1895 per point; all three plans beat it, with A3 roughly tripling its reach.

changes.change: In A3, drop popup:33C041EA on day 40 ($2500) and spend the money on podcast:17422834 (The Minimalists, $3350), trimming social:city slightly if needed to fit the budget.
changes.why: The pop-up earned 0.4% of credited adoption for $2500, while The Minimalists earned 7.1% in A2.

changes.change: Extend social:city in A3 from 30 days to start day 0 and run 41 days.
changes.why: City-wide ads are the second-largest driver and lift weak districts such as Fortnite/reggaeton and Stranger Things/K-pop, which sit at 16.6%.

changes.change: Move the Rich Roll podcast earlier, to around day 5.
changes.why: Earlier seeding gives more time for word of mouth, which already accounts for 56.1% of adoption.

changes.change: Do not use zone-only social:2 or social:3, or street teams, in the next round.
changes.why: In A1 these returned 0.6–1.5% of credited adoption for $450–$2460 each, far below the city-wide channels.

e.note: A3 is the strongest plan at 20.1% reach (P10 17.6%) for $694 per point, about 2.7x cheaper than the benchmark's $1895, driven by the Airbnb drop, city-wide social and Rich Roll. The day-40 Seven Sins pop-up ($2500 for 0.4% of credited adoption) and zone-only ads in A1 are poor value, and Fortnite/reggaeton and Stranger Things/K-pop districts lag at 16.6%.

e.text: Applying the Critic's notes: cut the late $2,500 party, add The Minimalists, start ads and Rich Roll earlier.

e.note: Revising: Revise A3: drop the day-40 Seven Sins pop-up party, add The Minimalists, start city social day 0 for 41 days, move Rich Roll to ~day 5. No zone-only ads or street teams. Variant 2: same but keep a cheap opening-weekend hook at the Roma Norte store itself (repair workshop/group run) instead of a second podcast if budget is tight.

e.text: B1 leads at 23.5% (bad-run floor 21%); checking if Narvarte and Santa María residents would actually show up.

e.note: Asking residents across the city

voices.name: Diego
voices.quote: I saw it on Instagram, I think, and then a friend mentioned the Airbnb thing. I already wear Patagonia stuff, so a sneaker that's actually made responsibly sounds right up my alley, I'd go to Roma for that.
voices.change: Trail or running models that hold up like my North Face shoes.

voices.name: Valeria
voices.quote: Honestly I only heard about it because an ad popped up while I was scrolling. I like simple stuff, Uniqlo kind of basics, so if they're clean-looking and not crazy expensive I might stop by.
voices.change: Minimal designs and a fair price; then I'd bring my roommate.

voices.name: Luis
voices.quote: Yeah, there was a poster about it at Seven Sins, right by the bar. I'm more into comfortable everyday shoes than hype drops, but Roma's close enough that I'd check it out on a Saturday.
voices.change: A good DJ set or event at the opening, Daft Punk vibes.

voices.name: Fernanda
voices.quote: I hadn't heard of it until now, to be honest. I usually just grab sneakers wherever I'm already shopping, so a special trip to a pop-up probably isn't for me.
voices.change: If they sold online or somewhere closer to Benito Juárez.

e.text: B1 wins: 23.5% reach, 21% floor, $14,980 — 3.5x the benchmark. Handing it to the Producer.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Early Airbnb drop plus two podcasts reaches about 23.5% of the natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is to start on day one with a co-branded Airbnb drop, follow with host-read ads on Rich Roll and The Minimalists, and run fit-weighted social city-wide so word of mouth builds before opening weekend. Qloo taste data shows this audience over-indexes strongly on Airbnb (0.95), Rich Roll (0.93) and The Minimalists (0.92), pulled in by Patagonia, Veja and Allbirds fans. In simulation the plan reaches 23.5% of the natural audience (range 21.0%–26.1%), about 3.5x the benchmark's 6.7%, at $638 per point of reach versus $1,895, with 58% of adoption from word of mouth; these are projections from a model built on Qloo data, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 41–35 before launch)
items: Day 41: launch the co-branded Airbnb drop and start fit-weighted social ads across Mexico City
Day 41: place posters and materials at El Regio Cortes y Hamburguesas and Seven Sins Mexico
Day 36: Rich Roll host-read ad airs; lead with responsible materials and Patagonia/Veja-style values

weeks.label: Week 2 (days 34–28)
items: Keep social running, shifting spend toward the best-performing fit cells
Push Airbnb drop content and reshares to fuel word of mouth

weeks.label: Week 3 (days 27–21)
items: Day 26: The Minimalists host-read ad airs; stress clean, minimal designs and fair price

weeks.label: Weeks 4–5 (days 20–11)
items: Social runs through day 11, then ends
Announce opening-weekend event at partner venues and online

weeks.label: Final stretch and opening (days 10–0)
items: Rely on word of mouth built up earlier; keep Airbnb drop visible
Open the Roma Norte pop-up; feature running/trail and minimal models, with a DJ set at the opening

risks: All figures are simulation projections on Qloo taste data; real reach may fall outside the 21.0%–26.1% range.
Reach lags in the Fortnite/reggaeton and Stranger Things/K-pop/Latin pop districts (about 20%).
The Minimalists ad and the two partners return the least per dollar; watch whether they earn their spend.
People unwilling to travel to Roma (e.g. Benito Juárez shoppers) may stay out without an online option.
measure: Airbnb drop engagement and referral traffic each week
Social ad click-through and cost per engaged visitor by district
Podcast promo-code or landing-page visits after each episode
Mentions and shares (word of mouth) and RSVPs for opening weekend
